chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Wahb ibn Hafsh from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you buy your sacrificial animal (Udhiyah) and wrap it, and it is placed beside your saddle, the sacrifice has reached its designated place; so if you wish to shave (its head), then shave it."

key_terms.قَمَطَ: To wrap or bind (specifically the animal's head/legs)

ai.seo_question: When does the Udhiyah sacrifice become valid and when can the animal be shaved?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the precise moment the Udhiyah attains its sacred status (Ihram) upon being secured beside the saddle. This ruling highlights the practical jurisprudence of the sacrifice, linking the physical preparation of the animal to the ritual permission for shaving, thereby emphasizing the sanctity of the offering in Shia legal tradition.
